indicators.note: foreign means strange or out of place, so the letters of the next word are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Something that points the way to diplomatic postings abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' looks like it describes the postings, but it tells you to rearrange POSTINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer showing direction is an indicator in the most literal sense.

indicators.note: on, in on board, places the food inside the ship letters

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, SS for steamship
tack is old slang for food, as in hard tack, the sailors' biscuit

explanation.surface: Piles of food on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the usual crossword signal for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks and heaps are both piles, and informally large quantities.

definitions.meaning: to ... someone in a subject is to prepare them with thorough basic teaching
a pitch for football or cricket is the playing field, a sports venue

explanation.surface: Getting the playing field ready for the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to instruct thoroughly in basics; the noun is a sports field.

definitions.meaning: a tablet fixed to a wall to mark a person or event
what a dentist means by the word is the film of bacteria on teeth

explanation.surface: A memorial plaque put up in honour of a dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorial tablets on buildings bear this name, as does the deposit dentists scrape off teeth.

clue.text: Storeman has talk about business with Banks, once

parts.note: to talk shop is to discuss your work, so shop is talk about business
Gordon Banks was England's goalkeeper in the 1966 World Cup, so once a keeper

explanation.surface: A warehouseman discusses work with a former banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests a financier, but it is Gordon Banks, the famous England goalkeeper of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman can mean someone who runs a store, which is what this retailer does.

clue.text: A place arranged for the bishop's residence

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters of the two words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: A suitable home has been found for the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the six letters of A PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's official home is traditionally called his palace, as at Lambeth.

clue.text: A friend writing SWALK is one of them

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or companion
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A pal writes SWALK on the back of a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: SWALK, 'sealed with a loving kiss', is written on British envelopes and is made from initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: SWALK is a word formed from initial letters, the defining feature of this class of word.

clue.text: In which real duty is abandoned!

definitions.text: In which real duty is abandoned!

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of the two words before are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A situation in which true obligation is cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: in infidelity, real marital duty is abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidelity in marriage is a betrayal in which the faithfulness owed to a spouse is forsaken.

clue.text: Try first to become a writer

parts.note: to essay something is to try or attempt it
first is written 1ST, and the 1 looks like I

explanation.surface: Making a first attempt at becoming a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST is read as IST, the figure one doubling as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An author of short prose compositions is a kind of writer.

parts.note: avocado is the name of a dull yellowish green, so a green of that kind is an avocado

explanation.surface: A piece of unripe fruit from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A green' reads as an adjective on the fruit, but avocado is itself a colour name; the fruit at the end of the clue is then the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocados are the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree; fruit can stand as a plural noun.

indicators.note: heartless means losing the heart, the middle letters of the hyphenated word that follows

explanation.surface: Unfeeling adults organise themselves into classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the central pair WN from GROWNUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups and classes are both categories into which things or people are sorted.

parts.note: the US state nicknamed the Bluegrass State is also home of bourbon whiskey; bluegrass is also a music style

explanation.surface: Asking where a country music style meets a whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: This American state is called the Bluegrass State and produces most of the world's bourbon.

definitions.meaning: gnarled means twisted and full of knobbly lumps, like old wood
a granny is a kind of knot, so something resembling one is full of knots

explanation.surface: An old woman described as twisted and gnarled.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood full of knots is gnarled; a granny knot is a common reef-knot mistake.

clue.text: They show frightening ability in their field

definitions.text: They show frightening ability in their field

parts.words: They show frightening ability in their field
parts.note: literally, figures whose job is scaring birds standing in a farmer's field, not experts in a profession

explanation.surface: Praise for people terrifyingly good at their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw figures stand in fields to frighten off birds, literally excelling at scaring there.

definitions.meaning: criteria are standards against which things are measured

explanation.surface: Asking what standards are used to judge magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard or reference point used for comparison and assessment.

clue.text: Radio set shaped like a star

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new form, so the letters of the two words before are remade

explanation.surface: A wireless set in the shape of a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' rearranges RADIOSET; the definition is the rarer adjectival sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means star-shaped, from the Greek for star.

indicators.note: disturbance means upsetting the order of things, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A discovery of drugs during trouble at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the pool with E and DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A finding is a judgement reached by a court or inquiry, which is a decision.

clue.text: Timon was one in a Neath scrum

indicators.note: a rugby scrum is a disorderly tangle of bodies, so the letters before it are tangled

explanation.surface: Timon caught up in a rugby scrum at Neath.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a Welsh rugby town; Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon lived in Athens, so he was a citizen of that city.

definitions.meaning: ducks is a British term of endearment for one person, like dear or love
a sweet with a heart, like a soft-centred chocolate

explanation.surface: Waterfowl that are soft inside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'ducks' (as in 'ta, ducks') is a singular affectionate form of address, so it matches a single beloved person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate names for a loved one, the northern English ducks and the general term.

clue.text: There's a lot about this in Hollywood

definitions.text: There's a lot about this in Hollywood

parts.words: There's a lot about this in Hollywood
parts.note: a lot is the land on which a film company's buildings stand, not a great deal

explanation.surface: Remarking that Hollywood has plenty of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A film company's production complex stands on its backlot, a Hollywood term for its grounds.

definitions.meaning: exact here is an adjective meaning precise and rigorous
a martinet is a stern disciplinarian, best described as severe

explanation.surface: A precise portrait of a tyrannical disciplinarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means precise and also demanding obedience to rules, as a martinet does.

indicators.note: get here means become something else, so the next word's letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to get high in a Belgian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stoned' reads as drug slang; 'Get' asks you to rearrange STONED.
explanation.definitionFit: The ferry port on the Belgian coast is a place in Belgium.

clue.text: English side won away from home

parts.note: a sports side such as a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
won, as in came first, means led

explanation.surface: An English team wins an away match.
explanation.walkthrough: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is the usual crossword shorthand for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exiled is banished and forced to live away from their homeland.

parts.note: transparent plastic sheets laid on an overhead projector to throw images onto a screen, not forecasts or protruding bits

explanation.surface: Paper used for drawing up projections, such as forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead projector transparencies are made of a plastic film named after its chemical base.

indicators.note: taking the even-numbered letters at regular intervals from the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Courtship happens even in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly even' takes the even-numbered letters only, and 'spring' is not the season but a source, the place a stream rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a source, the point where something rises or originates.

parts.note: read literally, the place beside the road; the surface phrase means incidentally

explanation.surface: An aside offered incidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge alongside a road or path is literally beside the way.

indicators.note: surrounding means going around something, so the shortened word encloses the little word before
almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter of the word after is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having a meal in a somewhat shabby setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter, and 'surrounding' puts the shortened word around the two-letter piece, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining is the act of having a meal, a more formal word for eating.

clue.text: A South Dorset organisation for divers

indicators.note: organisation means putting things in order, so the letters before it are reorganised

parts.note: Dorset is an English county on the south coast; its letters join the mix

explanation.surface: A club in south Dorset for people who dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people who dive but the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers, as an old-fashioned adjective, means several or of varied kinds, a synonym of mixed.
